documents.unit: Division of Information Resources & Technology and Office of the Provost
documents.title: Artificial Intelligence Policy (University Policies)
documents.summary: Rowan's university-wide AI policy (ISO:2024:01) is an information-security policy. It bans putting confidential data into public AI tools, requires approved platforms for university business, and covers procurement, AI meeting recording, copyright and research. For coursework it only points to the Academic Integrity Policy.
documents.stance_why: The policy is an information-security rule: it limits what data may enter AI tools and requires approved platforms for university business. It sets no stance on students' use of AI in coursework and sends coursework to the Academic Integrity Policy, so the stance is delegates. The words "AI requirements related to coursework must comply with the Academic Integrity Policy" show this.

units.why: The sentence sets the policy purpose: "establish requirements for the secure use of AI and Large Language Models". It states purpose and scope, so it is an institution-level framework (P56) rather than a rule on coursework.
units.anchor: establish requirements for the secure use of AI and Large Language Models

units.why: This sets who the policy binds: "all members of the Rowan Community who access and use the University's electronic information and information systems". It is scope, so P56.
units.anchor: applies to all members of the Rowan Community

units.why: The Provost and security officers "shall ensure compliance" with the policy; this names who owns and enforces it, so P80 rather than P56.
units.anchor: shall ensure compliance with this policy

units.why: "The Vice Presidents and Deans shall implement this policy" assigns implementation to named officers, which is P80 (who owns the policy).
units.anchor: The Vice Presidents and Deans shall implement this policy

units.why: "The use of AI tools must adhere to all Rowan University policies" requires AI use to follow existing university policy, which is P77 (comply with existing policy), not P45.
units.anchor: The use of AI tools must adhere to all Rowan University policies

units.why: Members "must adhere to ... ethical standards and policies of the University, with regard to data use, privacy, consent, ownership, and academic integrity", tying AI use to existing law and policy: P77.
units.anchor: must adhere to human resource and legal requirements, as well as ethical standards and policies
units.policy: must adhere to human resource and legal requirements, as well as ethical standards and policies of the University

units.why: Employees "should be aware of the requirements of the Open Public Records Act" and that AI meeting transcripts may be public records. This is a legal-compliance duty (P77); P86 does not fit because it is about consent to record, not records law.
units.anchor: AI generated transcripts of meetings may create records subject to OPRA

units.why: "must not enter Rowan internal, confidential, proprietary or regulated data ... into publicly-available AI tools, e.g. ChatGPT" bans a class of input to AI, to protect data: P50 (protect confidential data) fits better than P20, which is about assignment specs and student code.
units.anchor: must not enter Rowan internal, confidential, proprietary or regulated data
units.policy: Members of the Rowan community must not enter Rowan internal, confidential, proprietary or regulated data (finance, PII, ePHI, HR, student records, non-public research data) into publicly-available AI tools

units.why: "must only be processed in officially approved AI/LLM platforms" requires university business, including academic communications, to use approved tools; that is P92 (use approved tools institution-wide).
units.anchor: must only be processed in officially approved AI/LLM platforms

units.why: "No University business information may be processed on any unapproved platform" is a flat ban on unapproved platforms for university business, justified by data discoverability; coded P92 as the same approved-tools rule.
units.anchor: No University business information may be processed on any unapproved platform

units.why: "Subscriptions and purchases of AI services must be procured through the standard processes" of IRT and Contracting sets institutional control before purchase: P65.
units.anchor: Subscriptions and purchases of AI services must be procured through the standard processes

units.why: "Internal and closed meetings may only be recorded by AI platforms that are authorized" restricts AI recording to authorized tools, so P86 (control of AI recording).
units.anchor: Internal and closed meetings may only be recorded by AI platforms that are authorized
units.fit_note: Requires IRT authorization of the recording platform rather than consent of participants.

units.why: "AI transcriptions of confidential Human Resources meetings ... should not be used" without prior HR permission is a permission requirement for AI transcription: P86.
units.anchor: AI transcriptions of confidential Human Resources meetings, including candidate interviews, should not be used

units.why: "AI requirements related to coursework must comply with the Academic Integrity Policy" sends coursework AI rules to the existing integrity policy rather than setting a rule: P77 (comply with existing policy).
units.anchor: AI requirements related to coursework must comply with the Academic Integrity Policy
units.fit_note: Also shows the policy leaves coursework AI rules to the Academic Integrity Policy and instructors.

units.why: "Questions regarding the use of AI or data mining tools should be directed to the ... Office of Ethics, Academic Integrity or Research" names the offices that field questions about the policy: P80.
units.anchor: Questions regarding the use of AI or data mining tools should be directed to
units.policy: Questions about AI or data mining tools go to the Rowan University Office of Ethics, Academic Integrity or Research, as appropriate
units.fit_note: Names where users ask questions, not who interprets or enforces.

units.why: "The use of AI may not infringe on copyright laws" with the University Copyright Policy is a rule on copyright of AI use: P52.
units.anchor: The use of AI may not infringe on copyright laws

units.why: "AI use in Research ... must be conducted in accordance with applicable policies and governing Research" defers research AI to existing research rules, which is P62.
units.anchor: AI use in Research, including the development of AI and other machine learning, must be
units.policy: AI use in Research, including the development of AI and other machine learning, must be conducted in accordance with applicable policies

units.why: "shall be subject to discipline up to and including dismissal" states the consequence of violating the policy. P37 (state penalties in advance) fits partly because the penalty is for violating a data-security policy.
units.anchor: shall be subject to discipline up to and including dismissal from the University
units.fit_note: Penalty is for violating the data-security policy, not for academic AI misuse.

units.why: "Any exceptions to this policy must be approved by the Information Security Office and Office of the Provost" names who grants exceptions: P80.
units.anchor: exceptions to this policy must be approved by the Information Security Office and Office of
units.policy: exceptions to this policy must be approved by the Information Security Office and Office of the Provost

documents.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence & Teaching
tiers: Option 1: No generative AI (violation of academic integrity)
Option 2: No generative AI (assignments are for developing and assessing skills)
Option 3: Some generative AI (support learning, cite, work must be the student's own)
Option 4: Generic statement (follow instructor guidelines; cite; unauthorized use may be cheating)
documents.summary: Faculty Center page from Academic Affairs. It says Rowan has no universal GenAI policy, recommends that every syllabus state its AI rules, and gives four sample statements. It also advises against AI detectors, describes how to follow up on suspected misuse, and links many outside resources.
documents.stance_why: The page states "The University does not have a universal generative AI policy" and lets instructors choose from sample statements that range from no AI to some AI, so no stance is set at the university level: delegates. The sample statements are options.

units.why: "The University does not have a universal generative AI policy" says plainly that no single rule applies, and "Instructors may select one of the following statements" hands the choice to instructors: P04.
units.anchor: The University does not have a universal generative AI policy

units.why: The Senate Task Force makes a recommendation that faculty include a clear statement in syllabi and Canvas on how AI may or may not be used, which is P09 (an AI statement in every syllabus), stated as a recommendation.
units.anchor: Faculty should include a clear and specific statement in their syllabi and Canvas

units.why: "Sample syllabus statements for varying usage of AI" offers a menu from no AI to some AI to generic wording, which sorts uses into named options (P05) though it does not say any one is required.
units.anchor: Sample syllabus statements for varying usage of AI in the classroom
units.fit_note: Options are sample wording, not formally named tiers.

units.why: "Faculty also might choose to list the ways that generative AI could be used on some or all assignments" lets instructors set the rule per assignment: P04.
units.anchor: Faculty also might choose to list the ways that generative AI could be used

units.why: Option 1 says "any use of generative artificial intelligence ... will be considered a violation of academic integrity", a ban on all work in the course: P01.
units.anchor: any use of generative artificial intelligence such as ChatGPT, DALL-E, Claude, Copilot, Gemini, and others
units.policy: any use of generative artificial intelligence such as ChatGPT, DALL-E, Claude, Copilot, Gemini, and others will be considered a violation of academic integrity

units.why: "students committing any act of academic dishonesty may fail the assignment, fail the course, or face other sanctions" lists penalties in the sample statement: P37.
units.anchor: may fail the assignment, fail the course, or face other sanctions

units.why: "Violations that result in a grade penalty must be reported to the Provost's Office" is a required reporting step: P81.
units.anchor: Violations that result in a grade penalty must be reported to the Provost's Office

units.why: Option 2 explains that unauthorized AI "defeats the purpose, misrepresents your mastery of the material" of the assignments, a skill-building rationale: P41 (chosen over P43 because the main claim is that AI shortcuts the practice).
units.anchor: defeats the purpose, misrepresents your mastery of the material

units.why: Option 2 also classifies such use as "an academic integrity violation", which treats unauthorized AI as misconduct: P36.
units.anchor: is considered an academic integrity violation

units.why: "If you have questions about what resources may be allowed on a specific assignment please let me know" tells students to ask the instructor when unsure: P10.
units.anchor: If you have questions about what resources may be allowed on a specific assignment please
units.policy: If you have questions about what resources may be allowed on a specific assignment please let me know

units.why: Option 3 says AI "can be used as a tool to support learning (e.g., in obtaining feedback or generating ideas)", permitting feedback and idea generation; P15 is chosen because ideas are named, with feedback as extra (fit_note).
units.anchor: generative AI can be used as a tool to support learning (e.g., in obtaining feedback
units.policy: generative AI can be used as a tool to support learning (e.g., in obtaining feedback or generating ideas)
units.fit_note: Also permits AI for obtaining feedback, which no single type covers.

units.why: "work submitted by a student should be that of the student and not the work of an AI system" bars AI-produced submissions: P19.
units.anchor: work submitted by a student should be that of the student and not the work
units.policy: work submitted by a student should be that of the student and not the work of an AI system

units.why: "If you include material generated by an AI program, it should be cited like any other reference material" requires citation of AI material: P24.
units.anchor: it should be cited like any other reference material

units.why: "the student bears responsibility for any inaccuracies or misinformation" makes students answerable for AI errors in their work; P29 (own what you submit) is chosen over P31 because it does not tell students to verify.
units.anchor: the student bears responsibility for any inaccuracies or misinformation
units.fit_note: Names responsibility for AI inaccuracies; no instruction to verify.

units.why: "please reach out to your instructor" for questions on how AI may be used within the academic integrity policy: P10.
units.anchor: please reach out to your instructor

units.why: The generic statement says students "must follow all instructor guidelines on the use or prohibition of generative AI", making each instructor's rule binding: P78 (follow each course's rules).
units.anchor: you must follow all instructor guidelines on the use or prohibition of generative AI

units.why: "The unauthorized use of generative AI on assignments may be considered cheating" classifies unauthorized use as misconduct: P36.
units.anchor: The unauthorized use of generative AI on assignments may be considered cheating

units.why: "Submitting the output of generative AI without citation is considered plagiarism" makes missing disclosure the violation: P28.
units.anchor: Submitting the output of generative AI without citation is considered plagiarism

units.why: "you are responsible for any inaccuracies or information within your submitted assignments" holds students answerable for submitted content: P29.
units.anchor: you are responsible for any inaccuracies or information within your submitted assignments

units.why: "please do not hesitate to reach out to your instructor for clarification" encourages students to ask: P10.
units.anchor: please do not hesitate to reach out to your instructor for clarification

units.why: "Syllabi Policies for Generative AI Repository" is offered "to help other instructors see the range of policies" before writing their own; it supports instructors in learning about policy options: P63.
units.anchor: helping other instructors see the range of policies available by other educators

units.why: "Introduction to AI Literacy for Students is a Canvas module designed specifically for Rowan students" that faculty can add to courses: a student AI-literacy training resource, P70.
units.anchor: Introduction to AI Literacy for Students is a Canvas module designed specifically for Rowan students

units.why: The "Rowan-produced video" on student use of generative AI "can be shown in class or linked in your Canvas course(s)", a suggested way to explain AI expectations to students: P66.
units.anchor: This Rowan-produced video (2:20) can be shown in class or linked in your Canvas course(s)
units.fit_note: Offers a ready-made video rather than the instructor's own reasons.

units.why: The 2026 Student Guide "contains downloadable Teacher Guides ... that can be adapted for courses in any discipline", AI-literacy material for the community: P70.
units.anchor: downloadable Teacher Guides (pdfs & PowerPoints) that can be adapted for courses in any discipline

units.why: The page points to "Rowan-licensed GenAI tools and guidelines for using them", the university-approved tool list: P92 (institution-wide, not a single course tool).
units.anchor: an overview of Rowan-licensed GenAI tools and guidelines for using them

units.why: "The AI-Resistant Pedagogy Studio: An Interactive Toolkit for Assignment Redesign" is listed as a resource for faculty redesigning assignments; it helps instructors learn how to respond to AI: P63.
units.anchor: An Interactive Toolkit for Assignment Redesign

units.why: "we do NOT recommend relying on any of the numerous AI Content Detector programs" is advice against detectors, with reasons (not accurate, false positives): P39.
units.anchor: we do NOT recommend relying on any of the numerous

units.why: "Such programs have not yet demonstrated their accuracy" gives the reason detectors are not trusted, a limit on verification: P82.
units.anchor: Such programs have not yet demonstrated their accuracy and do not provide hard evidence for
units.policy: Such programs have not yet demonstrated their accuracy and do not provide hard evidence for evaluation
units.fit_note: Limits of detectors specifically; the type names limits of control in general.

units.why: "results from these detectors will not be considered as evidence for a Rowan Report of an Academic Integrity Violation" is a firm rule that detector output is not evidence: P39.
units.anchor: results from these detectors will not be considered as evidence for a Rowan Report of
units.policy: results from these detectors will not be considered as evidence for a Rowan Report of an Academic Integrity Violation

units.why: "other forms of evidence may be used to make a report" allows non-detector evidence in a report; it concerns what evidence counts, so P69 (the nearest type), though it names no standard.
units.anchor: other forms of evidence may be used to make a report
units.fit_note: No standard of proof is given; only says other evidence may be used.

units.why: AI "may create fictitious citations" and "hallucinate" quotes; this tells instructors that AI output can be wrong: P31 informs.
units.anchor: may not cite them correctly or may create fictitious citations

units.why: "fabrication is a form of academic dishonesty, faculty can submit Academic Integrity Violations based on invented sources" makes invented sources grounds for a report, i.e. evidence of misuse: P69.
units.anchor: faculty can submit Academic Integrity Violations based on invented sources and/or quotations
units.fit_note: Names one kind of evidence (invented sources) rather than a standard.

units.why: "faculty must file an AIV report if they wish to sanction a student" is a required procedural step: P81.
units.anchor: faculty must file an AIV report if they wish to sanction a student

units.why: "Schedule a time to discuss the topic of the paper with the student and ask follow up questions to verify their understanding" tells instructors to talk with the student first: P57.
units.anchor: Schedule a time to discuss the topic of the paper with the student

units.why: "Ideally, this would be built into the course structure so students are not singled out" suggests checking understanding of all students as part of the course: P34.
units.anchor: built into the course structure so students are not singled out

units.why: "initiate the discussion in a nonconfrontational manner" gives guidance on how to hold the follow-up talk: P57 with a fit note since the type is about talking first, not tone.
units.anchor: initiate the discussion in a nonconfrontational manner
units.fit_note: Adds the manner (nonconfrontational) of the conversation.

units.why: The Montclair resource is described as noting "no software is able to detect AI-generated content with 100% certainty", an acknowledgment that AI use cannot be fully verified: P82.
units.anchor: no software is able to detect AI-generated content with 100% certainty

documents.title: GenAI at Rowan: For Students
documents.summary: Library guide for students. It lists Rowan-approved GenAI tools with data-protection notes, warns that unpermitted use may be an integrity violation, tells students to check the syllabus or ask the instructor, and links citation and AI-literacy resources.
documents.stance_why: The guide tells students to follow each instructor's rules and that use without instructor permission may be an integrity violation, but it sets no rule itself and leaves permission to instructors. Hence delegates: "it is important to follow the guidelines given by your instructor for a specific course".

units.why: The guide says the tools "are approved by Rowan in terms of data protection", pointing students to the university-approved tool list: P92.
units.anchor: The tools below are approved by Rowan in terms of data protection

units.why: "it is important to follow the guidelines given by your instructor for a specific course" makes students responsible for each instructor's rules: P78.
units.anchor: it is important to follow the guidelines given by your instructor for a specific course

units.why: "Using GenAI in a course without the permission of the instructor may lead to an academic integrity violation" sets a default of no AI unless permitted. That is the fallback rule (P06) rather than a ban (P01), since permission can be given.
units.anchor: Using GenAI in a course without the permission of the instructor may lead to an
units.policy: Using GenAI in a course without the permission of the instructor may lead to an academic integrity violation

units.why: "serious sanctions attached" says unpermitted AI use carries serious sanctions, amounting to a statement that it is misconduct: P36.
units.anchor: have serious sanctions attached
units.fit_note: Sanctions are not specific.

units.why: "Be sure to check the syllabus" tells students to find out the course rule themselves: P78.
units.anchor: Be sure to check the syllabus

units.why: "clarify with your instructor whether they allow the use of such tools" tells students to ask the instructor: P10.
units.anchor: clarify with your instructor whether they allow the use of such tools in a course

units.why: "GenAI tools may confidently state false information, make up facts, quotations and citations" warns that output can be wrong: P31.
units.anchor: GenAI tools may confidently state false information, make up facts, quotations and citations

units.why: "be sure to engage carefully and thoughtfully with the generated content" asks students to evaluate AI output critically: P31.
units.anchor: be sure to engage carefully and thoughtfully with the generated content

units.why: Copilot is "available for students through their Rowan email address with commercial data protection. Student data is not used to train" the models: a data-protection fact about a vetted tool, P50.
units.anchor: Student data is not used to train the underlying language models

units.why: "there is currently no way to delete Gemini chats in Workspace accounts" warns students about data retention in a vetted tool: P50.
units.anchor: there is currently no way to delete Gemini chats in Workspace accounts

units.why: Firefly is "available for students who are enrolled in some College of Communication & Creative Arts courses", a licensed tool with limited availability: P92.
units.anchor: available for students who are enrolled in some College of Communication & Creative Arts courses

units.why: The guide covers "how to use GenAI tools approved by Rowan, cite AI-generated content, and uphold academic integrity" and links APA and MLA citation formats, so it points students to AI citation guidance: P24.
units.anchor: cite AI-generated content, and uphold academic integrity
units.fit_note: Gives links to citation styles; does not itself require citation.

units.why: The Student Guide "provides 7 principles to help with learning about GenAI as well as appropriate use" and is "recommended by Rowan"; it offers student AI-literacy material: P70.
units.anchor: provides 7 principles to help with learning about GenAI as well as appropriate use

documents.title: Generative AI Use Policy
documents.date_or_term: cites AI tools accessed June-July 2025; no explicit date
documents.summary: Departmental policy of Rowan's ECE department (an engineering unit that includes computer engineering). It lists appropriate uses (learning, brainstorming, debugging with at most 25% AI code, proofreading) and inappropriate ones (graded answers, data analysis, reports, uploading course material). It sets a detailed citation format and a process for suspected misuse that relies on oral or written explanation.
documents.stance_why: The ECE policy says it "welcomes, even encourages, responsible and educational use" of AI for learning, brainstorming and debugging, but only if AI content is not submitted as graded work; it allows up to 25% AI code and bans AI for answers, analysis, and reports. This is a permission with conditions and listed bans: permit.

units.why: "ECE department welcomes, even encourages, responsible and educational use of Generative AI" sets an encouraging default, so P02.
units.anchor: ECE department welcomes, even encourages, responsible and educational use of Generative AI

units.why: "so long as the AI generated content is not submitted as graded work" is the limit on the welcome: AI may not produce submitted work. P19.
units.anchor: so long as the AI generated content is not submitted as graded work

units.why: "All students ... are ultimately responsible for describing, justifying and/or explaining their work", the "primary mechanism" for judging authorship: P30 (explain your work).
units.anchor: All students (and, in fact, all engineers) are ultimately responsible for describing, justifying and/or explaining
units.policy: All students (and, in fact, all engineers) are ultimately responsible for describing, justifying and/or explaining their work

units.why: "When used responsibly, G-AI tools can be extremely helpful in retrieving information, solving routine problems, and learning" names benefits of AI: P87.
units.anchor: G-AI tools can be extremely helpful in retrieving information, solving routine problems, and learning new
units.policy: G-AI tools can be extremely helpful in retrieving information, solving routine problems, and learning new information

units.why: "improper use of G-AI tools can lead to inaccurate information as well as limit your ability to understand and apply important content" says misuse undermines learning: P41.
units.anchor: improper use of G-AI tools can lead to inaccurate information as well as limit your
units.policy: improper use of G-AI tools can lead to inaccurate information as well as limit your ability to understand

units.why: "prepare you not just for today's but also the future's job market ... where the need for appropriate use of these tools will be all too common" gives the career reason for teaching appropriate AI use: P44.
units.anchor: prepare you not just for today's but also the future's job market and workforce

units.why: "the need for human experts who can verify the accuracy of the G-AI output" says experts must check AI output: P31.
units.anchor: human experts who can verify the accuracy of the G-AI output
units.fit_note: Framed as a career need rather than a student duty.

units.why: "ECE graduates work in classified, confidential, or content-controlled areas, where the use of AI is strictly restricted" is a career reason to learn "how and when to use AI tools properly": P44 with a fit note, since it argues for correct use under restriction, not just AI skill.
units.anchor: a much larger portion of ECE graduates work in classified, confidential, or content-controlled areas
units.fit_note: Career argument is for restricted-AI workplaces, so it also resembles P94.

units.why: "Unless explicitly stated otherwise in a course syllabus, the following applies uniformly" sets what applies when the syllabus is silent (and lets a syllabus override): P06.
units.anchor: Unless explicitly stated otherwise in a course syllabus, the following applies uniformly
units.fit_note: The department rule is the default; a syllabus may state otherwise.

units.why: "to all undergraduate and graduate-level ECE courses" defines the scope of the department policy: P56.
units.anchor: all undergraduate and graduate-level ECE courses
units.fit_note: Scope is a department, not the whole institution.

units.why: Appropriate use includes "Research or learn something new, and/or help your own learning and understanding of any topic", a tutor-like use: P12.
units.anchor: Research or learn something new, and/or help your own learning and understanding of any topic

units.why: Appropriate use includes "Idea brainstorming for projects, proposals, discussion points": P15.
units.anchor: Idea brainstorming for projects, proposals, discussion points

units.why: Literature searches to suggest or summarize papers are allowed if the final synthesis is the student's and citations are "confirmed from verifiable and reputable sources". No type covers AI for literature search, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Literature searches to suggest papers or summarize academic content
units.uncovered_note: AI may be used for literature searches provided the synthesis is the student's and citations are verified in reputable sources.

units.why: AI "debugging your code" is acceptable under the stated condition; the sentence is coded P13 for debugging, with the code-share cap in the next unit.
units.anchor: For starting or creating a general/routine structure for coding, and/or debugging your code
units.fit_note: Also permits AI for starting a routine code structure.

units.why: "the substantial/vast majority (75% or higher ...) of the code is yours" sets a percentage cap on AI-generated code: P16 (code under stated conditions).
units.anchor: the substantial/vast majority (75% or higher, not counting the documentation part) of the code is
units.policy: the substantial/vast majority (75% or higher, not counting the documentation part) of the code is yours

units.why: "you understand, test, and document the code entirely and thoroughly" requires students to understand all AI-assisted code: P30.
units.anchor: *you* understand, test, and document the code entirely and thoroughly
units.fit_note: Adds testing and documenting, not only understanding.

units.why: "You will be asked to explain your code and demonstrate your understanding" says authorship is checked by explanation: P34.
units.anchor: You will be asked to explain your code and demonstrate your understanding

units.why: "Routine proof-reading for correcting grammar, typos ... so long as the original sentences are yours" permits AI for proofreading: P91.
units.anchor: Routine proof-reading for correcting grammar, typos, clarifying or correcting sentences

units.why: "Generating non-technical figures to be used as concept illustrations (subject to course-specific permissions)" allows AI-made figures; no type covers AI for illustrations, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Generating non-technical figures to be used as concept illustrations
units.uncovered_note: AI may be used to generate non-technical figures as concept illustrations, subject to course permission.

units.why: "Any assignment or exercise where the instructor specifically and explicitly asks you to use an AI tool" is appropriate: AI use built into an assignment, P79.
units.anchor: where the instructor specifically and explicitly asks you to use an AI tool

units.why: "If you are unsure whether a particular G-AI use case is appropriate, please reach out to your course professor" tells students to ask: P10.
units.anchor: please reach out to your course professor

units.why: "Any use of a G-AI tool that is not properly and thoroughly cited" is "inappropriate and not allowed", making uncited use banned: P24 (disclose with each submission).
units.anchor: Any use of a G-AI tool that is not properly and thoroughly cited

units.why: "Solving or answering any questions in any graded assignment, quiz, exam, or report" is listed as not allowed: no AI-made answers to graded work. P19 is chosen over P22 because it covers assignments and reports too.
units.anchor: Solving or answering any questions in any graded assignment, quiz, exam, or report
units.fit_note: Also covers quizzes and exams.

units.why: "Analyzing data, drawing conclusions based on experiments or data analysis" in graded work is not allowed. P89 permits data analysis; this is the reverse and no type bans it, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Analyzing data, drawing conclusions based on experiments or data analysis
units.uncovered_note: AI may not be used to analyze data or draw conclusions from experiments for graded work.

units.why: "Answering any essay-type questions ... in any graded assignment, quiz, exam, or report" bars AI-produced text answers: P19.
units.anchor: Answering any essay-type questions

units.why: Design courses may not use AI for "Determining impact factors, ethical and professional considerations" that ask students to "articulate your design decisions, professional judgment". The student must do the thinking: P32 with a fit note.
units.anchor: Determining impact factors, ethical and professional considerations for any design-related course
units.fit_note: Names design judgment and ethics reflection in specific courses.

units.why: "Code or code fragments that exceed 25% of the total script" is not allowed, a cap on AI-generated code that mirrors the 75% rule: P16.
units.anchor: Code or code fragments that exceed 25% of the total script
units.fit_note: States the cap from the prohibitive side.

units.why: "modifications or additions cannot be AI-generated and must all be your work" bars AI from changes to instructor-provided base code: P19.
units.anchor: the modifications or additions cannot be AI-generated and must all be your work

units.why: "Uploading class/course material, lecture notes to any unauthorized G-AI tool" is not allowed: P49.
units.anchor: Uploading class/course material, lecture notes to any unauthorized G-AI tool

units.why: "Mathematical derivations submitted as part of a graded assignment, quiz, exam, or report" may not be AI-made: P19.
units.anchor: Mathematical derivations submitted as part of a graded assignment, quiz, exam, or report

units.why: "Algorithm design submitted as part of a graded assignment, quiz, exam, or report" may not be AI-made: P19.
units.anchor: Algorithm design submitted as part of a graded assignment, quiz, exam, or report

units.why: "Using AI to generate any part or section of a lab report, project report, or any other submission" is not permitted, including report generation from raw data: P19.
units.anchor: Using AI to generate any part or section of a lab report, project report, or
units.policy: Using AI to generate any part or section of a lab report, project report, or any other submission

units.why: "uploading raw data, results, or incomplete notes into AI to generate a report is not permitted" bans feeding work material to AI to make a report: P20 fits partly (own data and notes rather than specs or code).
units.anchor: uploading raw data, results, or incomplete notes into AI to generate a report is not

notes: Coder B. Rowan has no university-wide academic-use AI policy (Faculty Center says so); the university AI Policy is an information-security rule. No school-level document found. The deferred instructor syllabus and the irt-aipolicy cached text were not coded because they are not included in the collect file. Data-analysis bans (2 units, ECE) were left UNCOVERED because P89 only covers the permit side; a candidate type is a ban on AI for data analysis or interpretation. Literature search and concept-figure permissions are also UNCOVERED.
